title: Adopting a Neglected Sibling Group
paragraphs: When three siblings faced separation into different foster homes after losing both parents, most prospective foster families declined to take all three together, citing the significant challenges of caring for multiple children simultaneously.
Hana and her husband, already raising two children of their own, made the unusual decision to take in all three siblings rather than allow them to be separated during an already traumatic period.

The adjustment period proved genuinely difficult, with five children under one roof requiring far more patience, resources, and emotional energy than either parent had initially anticipated when making their decision.
Financial strain became a real concern, and Hana took on additional freelance work in the evenings simply to cover the unexpectedly increased household expenses that came with the larger family.
Despite the difficulties, all three siblings gradually settled into the household, and years later, remain close not only to each other but to the two children who were already part of the family.

Hana rarely discusses the decision as remarkable, simply noting that keeping the siblings together felt like the only acceptable choice available to her, regardless of the practical difficulties it introduced.
